## How the course works

Each core section is planned to combine short asynchronous teaching, background materials, a **two-hour live call**, and a practice exercise. The five calls account for **ten hours of live teaching**. Introduction time, asynchronous work, exercises, and final-project work add to that total.

The first foundation lesson retains its deeper treatment of model training and inference. Its duration remains open; the general 10–15-minute video proposal does not establish a cap for that lesson.

Exercise completion is intended to support progression. Acceptance rules, retries, and the platform for recording completion are still being designed. These static materials provide a learning sequence; they do not enforce an unlock.

## The work builds across sections

Keep one working research space as the course develops. Add authority boundaries, apply a useful workflow, review its operation, and examine its wider data and governance implications.

[Final-project expectations](project.qmd) describe how that work can become a reproducible research pipeline.
